correctness.rationale: The affine pieces join and the periodic extension has degree one, displacement in [0,m], equality at 0 and 1/2 for the respective extremes, and mean sup displacement exactly one. Independently of the cited rotation theorem, on J=[0,1/2] the active increasing branch admits two inverse branches g_d(t)=(t+md)/(2m+1) for d=0,1 with disjoint images in J. Nested inverse intervals realize every binary sequence; the lift after k active steps exceeds the bounded residual coordinate in J by m times the number of ones in the first k digits. Choosing any limiting digit frequency and using N_n/n→1/m gives every ordinary rotation value in [0,1] on a single full-measure base set. The global displacement bound excludes any other upper rotation value. At time n the sample Bowen metric equals the deterministic metric of length N_{n−1}+1 because the sampled activation counts visit every intervening integer. These lengths go through all positive integers on the full-measure set, and their ratio to n tends to 1/m, proving the exact separated-set entropy rescaling at each fixed scale and in the limit. The inverse cylinders give 2^k separated points at a fixed scale for the deterministic map, while its Lipschitz bound 2m+1 gives the covering upper bound log(2m+1). Thus each member is positive and per-step entropy tends to zero with both controls fixed.
residual_risks: The uploaded finite script was not run. Contrary to the optional check description in RESULT.md, its final loop checks positivity of the upper bound rather than strict decay; neither the proof nor the counterexample depends on that check.

value.rationale: The example gives a boundary for quantitative extensions of the random rotation-interval positivity theorem. Width alone cannot quantify entropy, and even the natural first-moment integrability norm does not prevent rare large active steps. Both proposed controls are kept exactly fixed, not merely uniformly bounded on a degenerating family. This explains why a recurrence or stronger uniform control matters.
residual_risks: No recurrence-based lower bound is tested or ruled out, and the construction does not keep a common almost-sure displacement or regularity bound.
